Subject: Discovery recap + proposed next step (Veridian)

Hi Ellie / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today — great to learn about the scheduling, data residency constraints, and the three KPIs you’re trying to improve on the claims pipeline. I promised a short recap and a suggested next step, so here it is.

What we heard
- Primary goal: reduce end-to-end claim adjudication time by 20% within Q4.
- Constraints: must run in a VPC, SOC 2 evidence required, and limited capacity for vendor pilots (one business unit at a time).
- Success metric: 20% token reduction in manual triage plus latency < 300ms P95 for PDF extraction flows.

How Redwood could help (short)
- Private deployment or Dedicated capacity to meet VPC/SOC2 needs.
- KV caching + prefix routing to keep P95 latency low for short document flows.
- Intelligent batching to keep unit costs predictable for high-volume ingestion.

Proposed next step
- 30-minute technical alignment with your infra lead to validate VPC/KMS constraints + confirm a pilot scope (1 BU, 4-week pilot). I’m available next week on Tue/Wed afternoon PDT.

Attached: discovery-notes-20270728.pdf (brief call notes) and a one-page MAP-template.xlsx for mutual actions.

If this sounds off, tell me — I want to be respectful of timing and priorities. If it sounds reasonable, what’s the best way to lock a time with your infra or procurement stakeholders?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
